perspective:
From Harold Padilla’s perspective, he has access to the following:

- He is a project manager. His project team appears unmotivated, progress is suffering, and he feels frustrated, anxious, and at his wit’s end.
- He arranged a coffee-shop meeting with Arthur, whom he treats as a friend/advisor. He told Arthur his team seemed unmotivated and that he needed advice.
- He heard Arthur ask whether he had tried understanding what drives each team member. Harold admitted he had focused on project goals and deadlines, not personal motivations.
- He heard Arthur advise one-on-one conversations and making people feel valued and understood. Harold left feeling hopeful and relieved and planned to try it.
- In a team meeting, Harold proposed quick one-on-one chats. He heard Team Member 1 say it could be helpful and Team Member 2 say they were open to it. Harold said he would schedule time with each person and work together for project success.
- After implementing the advice, Harold observed that the team still was not responding well. He felt disappointed and worried and told Arthur this.
- He heard Arthur suggest there might be deeper issues such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors. Harold accepted this and decided to set up another round of meetings.
- In one-on-one meetings, Harold asked about concerns. He heard Team Member 1 say there was tension between a few people affecting work. He heard Team Member 2 say they felt overwhelmed by workload and stressed, making motivation hard.
- Harold told Team Member 1 he would look into resolving conflicts. He told Team Member 2 he would see about redistributing tasks and said their well-being was important.
- Harold felt optimistic and empowered. He believed addressing individual concerns would improve performance and intended to create a more supportive, open team environment through regular feedback sessions and team-building activities.
- He announced those changes to the team. He heard Team Member 1 say it sounded great and would help, and Team Member 2 agree that concerns were being addressed. Harold said their input and well-being were crucial to success.

He does not have access to other characters’ private thoughts, hidden motivations, or narrator-only descriptions beyond what he observed, heard, was told, or did himself.
